title: Component registry
description: The component registry, as defined in The Software Field Guide, issue #101: the estate's word — the packages it has admitted, each as a component, version, tier, and digest row. Judged at the package gate against the component package manifest, as a conformance gate: a package is in conformance when the registry carries a row for its component+version whose digest equals the artifact digest it publishes, every pinned dependency resolves to a registry row at exactly the pinned digest, and no customer-tier package depends downward. This schema mirrors the shape rules of the Rego validator (policies/component); the validator additionally enforces the semantic rules a JSON schema cannot — reviewedOn a real calendar date not in the future and not older than 365 days, one admission per component+version, and the five drifts judged at the join.

version.description: Version of the registry. Admission records are versioned like the estate that keeps them.

reviewedOn.description: Date the registry was last reviewed, YYYY-MM-DD. The validator flags reviews older than 365 days and dates in the future.

owner.description: The team that owns the registry. Admission records without an owner are records nobody maintains.

packages.description: The admitted packages, one row per component+version. The registry's digest is the estate's word; a package whose artifact no longer matches it has drifted from its registration.

version.description: The version admitted. Admission is per component+version, because the digest is.

hierarchy.description: The tier the estate registered the package at. The tier decides what may depend on it: customer-tier packages may build on it only if it is general or customer.

digest.description: The sha256 digest recorded at admission. A package whose published artifact digest no longer equals this row has drifted from its registration.
